claims.author: jonatack
claims.harm: guidance on multi-network node deanonymization is incomplete and potentially misleading, especially regarding Tor and I2P
claims.quote: As-is, (and it isn't your fault), I think this note is incomplete (and perhaps misleading).
claims.status_note: author deferred to investigate what could be added

claims.author: vasild
claims.quote: It is not "any" peer. That is, a single node being a recipient just sees an incoming transaction and they cannot tell if this is the originator or somebody relaying it.
claims.request: clarify that an actor with many connections to many nodes, rather than any peer, can correlate incoming transactions

claims.author: vasild
claims.quote: Even if a node runs only on Tor+I2P and thus has concealed their IP address, it still has some identity which is protected by `-privatebroadcast`.
claims.request: clarify that private broadcast protects the node's identity even if operating solely over Tor/I2P with a concealed IP

claims.author: vasild
claims.quote: regardless of this setting. Wallet-level private broadcast is not yet supported. I closed the issue: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/34476#issuecomment-6012629426
claims.request: note that wallet-level private broadcast is not yet supported and drop the tracking issue link since it was closed

claims.author: instagibbs
claims.quote: The core of the claim is that our node is meant to act the same as any other, that we will not tell our peers about the tx until we hear about it over p2p. We don't know if it reaches the "wider network", as the recipient may be an adversary.
claims.request: reframe private broadcast guarantees around ensuring the node acts like any other node rather than claiming to know if the transaction reaches the wider network
